messages:
carmen: FYI — customer-reported p99 spike hitting /v1/chat in ap-southeast-1 since ~2026-03-17T07:03Z. p95 jumped from ~90ms to ~700ms+ and some timeouts reported. Looks like TLS handshake retries and longer DNS lookups.

devon: seeing it on infra dashboards too. Is this global or APAC-only?

carmen: APAC only so far (ap-southeast-1). Sample from logs shows increased egress hop count + tls_retries.

carmen: ```[2026-03-17T07:03:50Z] request_id=abc123 path=/v1/chat latency=742ms tls_retries=3 egress_hop_count=6 dns_lookup=118ms pop=ap-southeast-1```

aj: @ops-oncall any recent route work?

deploy-bot: rollout: route-policy-v2 -> apac-pop completed at 2026-03-17T07:00:12Z by @ops-oncall :white_check_mark: 

ops-oncall: confirmed, we pushed route-policy-v2 to prefer new regional egress at 07:00 UTC.

devon: running traceroutes from probes now. early output looks like a long hop then latency collapses — possible cross-AZ hairpin.

devon: ```traceroute to api.redwood.com (1.2.3.4)
1 10.9 ms 10.8 ms 11.2 ms
2 12.4 ms 12.1 ms 12.3 ms
3 210.6 ms 211.4 ms 209.9 ms  <-- big cross-az hop
4 13.5 ms 13.1 ms 13.2 ms
5 14.0 ms 14.2 ms 13.9 ms```

maria: DNS logs show the VIP TTL changed from 300 -> 30 at 07:00 (matches rollout), GSLB may be rebalancing more aggressively now.

carmen: also getting TLS early_close and session resumption misses for the high-latency traces.

devon: quick mitigation idea — add a regional fallback to us-east1 for affected traffic while we triage. low-risk and should avoid the hairpin.

ops-oncall: applied temporary fallback -> regional:us-east1 at 2026-03-17T07:10:08Z. rolling back route-policy-v2 can be done if needed.

carmen: metrics after fallback: p95 fell to ~120ms within 3m. p99 trending down as well. customers confirmed improved experience. :thumbsup:

aj: nice. Short-term mitigation in place. Need RCA and postmortem. Who owns which part?

maria: I will take DNS/GSLB config and TTL changes. devon can own routing/topology and the cross-az behavior. carmen, please dump request traces/ids for us.

carmen: adding sample request ids: abc123, def456, ghi789 and links to traces in the incident graph (sent out-of-band).

srebot: alert 4519876543 suppressed by @carmen after mitigation.

devon: hypotheses: 1) route-policy-v2 introduced an anycast->regional handoff path that increases hop_count for some POPs, 2) TTL drop to 30 caused GSLB churn and transient route oscillation, 3) TLS session resumption fails across the handoff so clients pay full handshake on retry.

maria: next actions: revert canary of route-policy-v2 in apac, pin TTL back to 300, add canary test to detect hairpin/hop_count increase before wider rollout.

ops-oncall: followups for runbook: add `rbacctl set-route-fallback --region us-east1 --scope ap-southeast-1` as a one-line mitigation, add alert for sudden VIP TTL changes, and a kpi for egress_hop_count delta > 2.

carmen: customer update drafted: mitigation applied (fallback to us-east1), investigating root cause, ETA ~4h for RCA. Will post updates in thread.

aj: thanks all. Keep any critical traces/pcaps in the incident channel and tag me if latency spikes again.

maria: logged a follow-up ticket for GSLB config and a scheduled canary rollback test.

ops-oncall: leaving notes in the change log and will coordinate a safe rollout plan once we have fixes.
